nodes.characterization_summary: TEM analysis proves formation of amorphous phase and P vacancies in Co doped NiP catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co heteroatoms partly occupied the Ni sites, forming amorphous phase and P vacancies as proved by the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis (Fig. 6c–e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows decreased Pt-Pt radial distance due to compressive stress and increased Ni radial distance due to tensile stress in PtNi nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS measurement revealed that the radial distance of the Pt atom is decreased due to the compressive stress, and the radial distance of the Ni atom is increased due to the tensile stress.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms electron transfer between Ru and Fe/Co atoms in Ru single-atom FeCo-LDH catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS and EXAFS analysis confirmed electron transfer between Ru and Fe/Co and the formation of a Ru–O–Fe/Co coordination structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM imaging reveals Ru single-atoms breaking FeCo-LDH symmetry and introducing lattice defects (Fig. 8a–c).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image showed that the introduced Ru single-atom can break the symmetry structure of FeCo-LDH and introduce lattice defects (Fig. 8a–c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS confirms single-atom Ru creates O defects with electron transfer from W to Ru in Ru/WO3 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS and X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) analysis indicated that introduced single-atom Ru would create O defects and electrons would be transferred from W to Ru
